gold.title: Traces = event log (what happened), graph = state (what's true now) — no cross-boundary reconstruction
gold.content:
Clean architectural split for what the dashboard reads:

- **Traces are the event log** — what the system DID (every O/K/Δ, append-only, time-ordered). They own 'what happened.'
- **The graph (nodes/edges) is state** — what the system IS right now. It owns 'what's true now.'

A node's **creation** is an event (lives in the trace). A node's **current content** — after revision, healing, absorption, re-embedding — is state (lives in the graph). No single trace holds it; it's the fold of all deltas. Replaying traces to reconstruct state is lossy — traces store summaries and deltas-at-the-time, not current values.

**The drift principle:** drift only appears when a view answers an *event* question using *state* or vice-versa, OR when it reconstructs across that boundary with a heuristic. Three forms the brain has hit:
1. A separate parallel store → `brain_dashboard.db` (killed)
2. A maintained aggregate that drifts from its source → encoding counter (replaced with trace-pull)
3. Cross-boundary reconstruction → 'which nodes did this run create?' is an event question, answered with `encoding_source + ±2min` state heuristic (fixed by Fix B)

Rule: **each view reads the store that authoritatively owns its answer, and never reconstructs across that boundary with a heuristic.**
gold.situation: When designing dashboard views, deciding whether a view should read traces or graph, or debugging any dashboard data that appears to drift when code changes

**One question:** does using *more* of the brain's signals — not just "the cue looks like this memory" cosine — make recall surface the *right* memory more often? That's your standing thesis: *more, not less.*

We couldn't answer it before because **our measuring stick was rigged.** The old gold corpus was built by the same cosine lens we were trying to beat — so cosine always "won" by definition, and every other signal "lost." The verdict was circular; it meant nothing.

## The steps, simply

1. ✅ **Build an honest ruler.** The 24-cue gold — judged by blind Opus judges reasoning from *what actually happened next*, not from what cosine retrieved. (That's the strange-newton work we preserved.)

Episodic reaches a different way: *"find past conversations like this one, pull the memories that came out of them."* `nodes_for_traces` is the tool for exactly that. The test: **does it reach gold that cosine misses?**

4. ⏭ **Keep what wins, compose into one recall.** Every signal that earns its place on the honest ruler goes into the combined recall.

First, how the clusters enter the harness:
- `ess` = **Gold+ ∪ Gold flattened into one set of node-ids** (96 nodes across 24 cues).
- `gplus` = the Gold+ set only (16 nodes).
- `needs` = the gold items **grouped by the judge's `need` text** → `need → {node_ids}`. This is the real equivalence cluster: the judges picked *different node IDs for the same knowledge* (`837104d0`), so surfacing **any** node in a need's set = that need is met. These needs span tiers.

Then:

| metric | how it's computed | what it answers |
|---|---|---|
| **hit@5** (33%) | per cue: did **any** node in `ess` land in top-5? avg over 24 cues | "got *at least one* needed thing" — **tier-blind, lenient** |
| **Gold+@5** (17%) | same, but only over the `gplus` cluster | "got a *high-confidence* node" — strict |
| **need@5** (13%) | per cue: (#needs with ≥1 node in top-5) / (#needs); avg | "what *fraction of distinct needs* were met" — **the cluster-correct one** |
| **nDCG@5** | top-5 ranked list, gain = Gold+ 3 / Gold 2 / Silver+ 1.5 / Silver 1 | tier-graded ranking quality |

gold.title: Multi-judge variance finding: v1∩v2=∅ on node IDs, but judges agree on knowledge cluster — gold must be equivalence-set
gold.content:
Anchor ran a 5-cue comparison of two judge runs (v1 = old disjoint-field bundles, v2 = conversation-window bundles + episodic bridge instruction). Headline: **exact-node agreement = 4/23 node selections (17%). But on all 5 cues, both judges hit the same knowledge cluster.**

Per-cue analysis:
| cue | A∩B (exact) | why disjoint |
|---|---|---|
| operator_msg_0131 | 2 | both found cited-by-id nodes |
| operator_msg_1566 | 2 | both cited-by-id nodes agreed |
| operator_msg_0744 | 0 | both hit timeout cluster (different nodes) |
| anchor_turn_0681 | 0 | both found ground in community-routing cluster (diff nodes = equivalents) |
| anchor_turn_1155 | 0 | both hit severity-doctrine cluster (diff members) |

**The conclusion:** when a node is *cited by id* in the move, both judges agree (911bd283, c57ff45c, 32ab5545). When knowledge lives in an equivalence cluster, path-divergence in search means each judge finds *a different member of the set* — both correct, but not the same ID.

**Need-level reanalysis (Turn 7):** when scoring at the *need* (equivalence set) level rather than node level, Gold+ agreement spans ALL 5 cues — the node-lottery dissolves into need-consensus. Node-level Gold+ = 4 nodes on 2 cues; Need-level Gold+ = 7 distinct needs across all 5 cues. The judges *did* agree on cold-connection / communities-unused / severity needs — they just reached different nodes.

**Design consequence:** gold cannot be a single node ID — it must be the **equivalence set** (the knowledge cluster). Ensemble + union captures the full set. Adjudication collapses the union into canonical gold grouped by equivalence.
gold.situation: When interpreting any single-judge corpus or adjudicating ensemble gold results — node-ID agreement is low but knowledge agreement is high; the right gold unit is the equivalence set (the knowledge cluster), not a single node ID

HEADLINE -- THE PRIZE: the UNION of all realizable cues x mechanisms reaches 53% hit@5 / 64% hit@25, vs 19%/36% for cue-primary alone (what we use today). ~3x at hit@5. best-of(53) >> max-single(19) => the signals are strongly COMPLEMENTARY (different cues/mechanisms hit different gold). 22% is ORACLE-ONLY (only next_move/future surfaces it -> needs prediction); 14% UNREACHABLE (encode-gap, S11.1 bridges).

MATRIX READS:
- _primary is the best field for EVERY cue; content/situation/question/title/reasoning all underperform -> multi-FIELD matching is a dead end; the lever is multi-CUE not multi-field.

- oracle next_move 39%/64% ~2x best realizable.

The unlock is a per-cue SELECTOR/ROUTER that picks the right cue x mechanism. The regression quantifies the prize (~3x) and names the mechanism.

gold.title: Episodic-semantic linking: 3 methods Tom proposed — register-bridge, encode-timing, prev-anchor dual-operator
gold.content:
Tom's Turn 6 proposals for connecting episodic retrieval to semantic nodes — these are the methods that replace the failed ±2d temporal arm:

**Method 1 — Register bridge (cue → episode → node cosine):** Cosine(operator/anchor cue, past episodes) → for top-X matching episodes, cosine those episodes against semantic nodes. Rationale: the gold is a distilled *principle* (different register than the cue), but past episodes share the cue's conversational register AND are semantically tied to the nodes they produced. The episode crosses the register gap the direct hop can't. Risk: both hops run on the flat embedder — only works if episodes are genuinely better-matched than the direct cue. **STATUS: BUILT and empirically validated (cue seed axis — encoded/picked/dropped roles).**

**Method 2 — Encode-timing (cue → episode → next-encode nodes):** Cosine(cue, episodes) → for each top-X matching episode, pull nodes created/revised in the next encode or two after that episode's timestamp. This reconstructs the source_ref link via encode-cycle timing — works for OLD nodes where source_refs are 0%. Key caveat: verify the matched episode IS the gold's producer (the ±2d time-skew finding showed episodes can be 28–72 days from when the gold was encoded). **STATUS: UNBUILT.**

**Method 3 — Anchor prev-msg as dual operator:** Anchor's previous response → cosine with episodic → dual operator: inhibit the already-said neighborhood AND activate a new arc. The most flexible, lowest priority — build once Methods 1 & 2 are validated. **STATUS: UNBUILT.**

**Tom's framing:** 'these only show the complexity of LAF but also its flexibility' — these are LAF layers with different SOURCE (prev-anchor), different OPERATOR (activation, inhibition), demonstrating the grammar's expressiveness.

**Current state (2026-06-30):** only the cue→episode seed axis is built (Method 1 family). The three-role family (encoded/picked/dropped) runs on this single seed. The never-consolidate rule (see episodic-role-rule node) means each role gets its own gain row even within this one seed axis.

gold.content: The endo-recall research story crystallizes through a complete read-side falsification arc (June 17-18) that reframes recall from 'which algorithm is best' to 'how do we route multiple complementary signals.' The pattern: every isolated cosine lever (PPR 14-16%, content-episodic 7-8%, predictive-followup 3-5%, question-field 10%) underperforms the baseline (cue-cosine 22%) on a clean teacher-minted gold corpus (73 cues). The oracle even at 42% (perfect next-move query) proves the embedder is the ceiling. BUT the reverse-regression finding (id:8bcc8c96) reframes the wall: the realizable UNION of cues×mechanisms reaches 53% hit@5 on the SAME embedder—we use ~1/3 of available signal, and the cues are strongly complementary. The unlock is not a new embedder but a learned SELECTOR/router. Two-disease map: Disease A (within-cluster smear) has cheap levers (FTS rare-token, cross-encoder reranker, edge-inhibition); Disease B (cue-far) needs a next-move predictor or improved encoding. The session decided: build the selector next (handoff #2, id:117b6ad9); empirically validate per-disease cheap levers; run embedder bench in parallel (stream 06fe1193). Lesson: more signal not better algorithm; complementary routes not uniform fusion; measure before tuning.
gold.situation: When optimizing endo-recall or any multi-cue ranking system—don't choose 'the best algorithm'; route by signal type (cue, prev_operator, graph context) with a learned selector; measure which diseases your misses belong to (embedding gap vs ordering gap) before designing the fix.

gold.content:
The blind-judge pilot (8 cues, Turn 8) exposed three distinct failure modes the old lens-minted corpus was structurally blind to:

**1. Same-session echo** (op_0094, op_0118): The old gold for op_0094 included nodes the S1-scribe encoded *from the same session's turns, ~4 min before the cutoff* — their content is verbatim in the active conversation, so surfacing them helps nothing. cos_next mints them (topical bullseye because they reference what was just said); the blind judge dropped them and found the real *older* prior (the `iso_cutoff` wall-clock-vs-conversation rule). **Rule:** any node whose content echoes live conversation context at the time of the cue is a same-session echo — drop from gold.

**2. Reasoned-helpfulness over topic** (anchor_0087): The decisive nodes weren't the topically-nearest self-channel schema nodes — they were *cross-cutting conventions* ("close-the-class, don't patch"; "config = parameters not decisions"). Schema nodes → silver (Anchor already had the live contract); conventions → essential (the missing knowledge that would have changed the move). Topic-proximity is the lens-trap; reasoned-helpfulness is the standard.

**3. Content-graft time-leak** (anchor_0387): The old gold `a1364fc9` passes `created_at ≤ cutoff` — it was encoded before the cutoff — but its content was *edited months later* (references a commit ~3h after the cue) without bumping `revised_at`. At the cutoff, the node said the opposite ("edges are non-revisable"), which would have *confirmed Anchor's wrong instinct*. `created_at ≤ cutoff` does NOT catch this. The judge caught it, dropped it as essential=[], and correctly classified the decisive knowledge as an encode-gap. **Rule:** cutoff eligibility requires reasoning about what the node *said* at cutoff, not just when it was created.
gold.situation: When building a blind-judge corpus-construction protocol, reviewing gold candidates for legitimacy, or debugging why old lens-minted gold disagrees with human judgment — these three failure modes explain the 7/8 disagreement and each requires a distinct guard in the judge protocol

Tom's four questions in Turn 9 about the journal review block draft:
1. Does the stateless agent know what 'the brain' is?
2. Does it understand what 'next self' or 'operator' means?
3. Will 'anchor every note to what it's about' narrow notes (suppression/force-fit risk)?
4. Does the agent know what 'a trace' is?

**Empirical answer (from probe):** The probe had grounded all four terms in the framing — and Sonnet's V1 output showed it understood them (the locked-wall note referenced 'operator intervention' and 'the brain cannot self-heal this'). So 1/2/4 work in practice with Sonnet — but via inference, not explicit grounding. Fragile for weaker models.

**Q3 was the sharpest (and the one the probe didn't test):** Every probe scenario had a clean nameable subject by design. Two real failure modes the hard gate could cause:
- Suppression: diffuse-but-real residue ('this whole batch felt like low-value clusters') gets dropped for lack of a clean subject
- Force-fit: agent invents a vague subject to pass the gate (V2 showed `cluster signals` / `cluster scoring` as force-fit artifacts)

**Fix:** Subject gate broadened — 'the run itself' added as a valid subject anchor, so diffuse residue isn't dropped.

Good synthesis prompt. Let me give you my honest read of where the accumulated evidence lands — and engage each of your four, because two are right, one needs sharpening, and one (your #3) I clearly didn't explain well.

## What we understand, in one frame

Recall is **prediction-dominated**: 65% of the gold is *the answer the move concluded*, which lives near the **outcome**, not the cue. The cue holds the question; the gold holds the answer. So a realizable recall system has a **structural ceiling below the oracle gold by design** — and the engineering job splits cleanly into (a) a *stack of realizable operators* that recovers ~72% from the cue, and (b) a *predictor* for the ~28% the cue genuinely can't reach. Today production runs ~1.5 of the ~6 operators that stack needs. That's the gap.

Now your four:

## 1. The judges used the oracle — unfair but more accurate ✓ (and it's the *correct* design)

Right, and I'd push it one step further: the oracle isn't a flaw to apologize for — it's the **correct definition of gold** under "recall is prediction" (`ca840441`). The best recall for turn N is the one you'd write having seen N+1. So the hindsight *is* the point: it defines the prediction target accurately, where the old lens-minted gold only measured "what cosine finds."

The discipline it forces on us: **score realizable operators only against the realizable subset (72%), and treat the predictor-gated 28% as a separate target** — never penalize a ranking operator for failing to reach gold that no cue could reach. Both confirmed, precisely — and you're right on both.

## 1. The edge weight is a hardcoded `0.5` we never calibrated

Exact answer to "what is `SUM(weight)` on": `add_relation` defaults **`weight = 0.5`** (dal.py:3092) for every edge the encoder creates, and the encoder almost never passes an explicit one. The two things that *do* move weight are:
- **`decay_edges`** — `weight × 0.5^(hours/half_life)`, but only on relations flagged `decays` (the auto-generated ones), and
- **Hebbian strengthening** — only on **co-access**,

…and **both of those act on exactly the relation types the graph operator already excludes (the `noise` aspect).** So for the *semantic* edges the graph actually walks (`grounds`/`extends`/`corrects`/`implements`), the weight is just the **uncalibrated 0.5 default**. `SUM(weight)` ≈ `0.5 × (number of relations on the pair)` — it encodes **relation multiplicity, nothing more.** It is not a relevance signal, full stop.

So the rebuild drops stored weight entirely. The spread weight on each edge becomes **cosine-grounded**: `cos(cue, edge_description)` (the edge `why` — the signal the reverse-engineering said carries the need) × the seed node's activation, optionally × a *deliberately-set* relation prior (corrects/grounds up). Everything quantitative is cosine or something we actually compute — never the 0.5.

## 2. Haiku's pick *and* drop are both traced — your "real-time judge" is realizable

This is the better find. The surface step records more than what Haiku picked:
- the **O trace (`recall`)** = the full candidate pool, and
- the **K trace** carries `outcomes_per_candidate: {id: 'selected'|'dropped'}` and a `dropped` list.

So **"what Haiku picked vs didn't pick" is fully reconstructable from traces** — we have the rejections explicitly. And the weighting you asked for ("account it to the previous-5-turns and their similarity to now") is *exactly* what `recall_episodes` already gives: its cosine `_score` per matched past moment **is** the similarity between that moment's context and the current cue. That is a **real-time judge cached as a context-weighted prior** — Haiku already adjudicated "not worth surfacing here," and we transfer that verdict to similar situations now. gold.title: Edge weight sources: 7 creation paths, 3 strengthening triggers, decay defined but possibly inactive
gold.content:
Complete audit from this session. All 7 edge weight creation paths, 3 strengthening triggers, decay defined but inactive, and the critical fatigue/weight distinction.

**Creation (initial weight):**
| Source | Weight | Location |
|--------|--------|----------|
| Encoding agent creates edge | 0.5 default or explicit | `connect_typed()` → `EDGE_TYPES[type].defaultWeight` |
| `remember_batch` auto-connect | 0.5 | `brain_remember.py:1111` |
| `remember_batch` connect_to (fuzzy match) | 0.6 | `brain_remember.py:1132` |
| `recall_on_create` related matches | 0.4-0.6 | `brain_remember.py:1613-1638` |
| `brain_evolution` co_accessed promotion | 0.4-0.6 | `brain_evolution.py:251` |
| `brain_evolution` corrected_by override | **0.9** (highest automatic) | `brain_evolution.py:705` |
| MCP `connect` tool | 0.5 default or explicit | `connect()` param |

**Strengthening:**
| Trigger | Formula | Location |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `connect()` on existing edge | `min(1.0, old + 0.2 × 0.5)` = +0.1 per call | `brain_connections.py:48` |
| `connect_typed()` on existing edge | same formula | `brain_connections.py:99` |
| Hebbian (surface co-selection) | calls `connect()` on pairs → same +0.1 | `daemon_hooks.py:_hebbian_strengthen` |

**Decay:** Only for `co_accessed`, `emergent_bridge`, `exemplifies` (decays: True, halfLife: 720h). **Possibly not running** — defined but no active caller confirmed.

**CRITICAL DISTINCTION — Fatigue ≠ Weight:**
Synaptic fatigue dampens **node recall scores** (how likely a node appears in candidates), NOT edge weights. A hub node that surfaces every turn gets fatigued so it appears less. But its edges stay the same weight. These are independent systems — fatigue affects candidate selection, weight affects which connections show once a node is selected.

Edge fatigue (newly designed, not yet built) also does NOT change weight — it rotates which edges display within a session via a session-scoped counter. Weight mutation is S2's domain.

gold.title: Creator-label is set once at birth, never written again on updates
gold.content:
The architectural invariant for `encoding_source` on both nodes and edges: **a creator-label is set once, at the moment of first creation, and never touched again on subsequent updates or re-connections.**

This invariant already exists explicitly in `brain_connections.py:228-233` for edges: 'defaulting to anchor would silently clobber a field the caller never asked to change (e.g. an s2:reclassify edge becoming anchor on rename).' The `None`=preserve contract on `connect_typed` is the mechanical expression of this invariant.

S2 units *already* write their label onto re-touches (the same broad mechanism), which means the fix must apply uniformly: the correct rule is that a creator-label is set at birth, full stop — applying to both the anchor doorway (MCP) and the S2 doorway (daemon internals). The proxy-stamp approach broke this by injecting concrete values on update commands.

**Implementation:** stamp `encoding_source` only in the INSERT path (new node/edge creation), never in the UPDATE path. Read existing value and preserve it on re-touch.

Agent-assisted code review (Turn 7) surfaced three facts from the actual code that Anchor would have gotten wrong by guessing:

**1. The production rendering locus (confirmed):**
- Saturation at `surface_contract.py:1154`: `node_activation[target] = tanh(prior + incoming)` — sum > ~2 pins at 1.0.
- Ranking at `:1855-1859`: `sort_key = (node_activation, mean_field_activation, nid)` — primary key is saturated activation.

**2. HOP_SCRUTINY is OFF in production by default:**
`HOP_SCRUTINY_DEFAULT=False` — deliberately, because it traded latency for recall (per node `3188e601`). This means the per-hop narrowing that was supposed to contain the flood was never active in production.

**3. Arm C rebuild does NOT need kernel surgery:**
The `cluster` variant already tracks `convergence_count` (sources-per-target) at `:1405-1409`. 'Own-relevance × bounded multi-seed boost, no magnitude propagation' is expressible as a new variant on top of cluster: `rank by max(field_activation) × (1 + coeff·convergence_count)`. The rebuild is a variant, not a restructure.

**4. Stopgap tests pass by design:**
Pinning tests assert nodes activate and render, not rank order — so the sort_key swap doesn't break the test suite.

**5. Prior eval findings reconciled:**
Nodes `7367947d` (spread augmentations ruled out) and `21521f48` (narrowing neighbors to 15 hurt −4pp) measured COVERAGE/encoder-muster context, NOT inject-precision. Both can be true: spread's breadth genuinely matters (narrowing hurt); its ranking is broken (buries the answer). The stopgap preserves breadth, fixes rank.

before.op:
In servers/daemon_server.py, BrainDaemon._accumulate_touched (around line 785) reads `sess = args.get('session_id')` to pick which SessionContext.touched accumulator to mutate, then bails if falsy. This is the Piece 3a "Anchor touched" feature that flushes an anchor_touched S0 trace in daemon_hooks.post_response_common.

Problem: the MCP tool schemas in servers/brain_mcp.py do NOT carry `session_id` for the tools _accumulate_touched targets:
- Write tools (remember, remember_batch, revise, revise_batch, brain_batch) have no session_id property; their handlers resolve the caller via servers/dispatch_common.caller_session(args) = `args.get('session_id') or args.get(CALLER_SESSION_KEY)` where CALLER_SESSION_KEY='_caller_session'. The proxy (daemon_send/_stamp_caller_session) stamps identity under _caller_session, NOT session_id.
- get_node / get_nodes schemas declare only node_id/node_ids/rich — no session_id at all.

Result: `args.get('session_id')` is None for every tool _accumulate_touched cares about, so the whole accumulator never populates in production. The authored AND recalled relations in trace_links.nodes_for_traces are silently always-empty. Unit tests pass only because they append to ctx.touched directly, bypassing dispatch.

Fix: have _accumulate_touched resolve the session the same way write handlers do — `from servers.dispatch_common import caller_session; sess = caller_session(args)` — so it uses _caller_session when session_id is absent. Verify: writes via reme

Right — and that corrects a sloppy framing in my summary. I said the write tools "have no `session_id` property" as if it were a gap. It isn't. `_stamp_caller_session` (brain_mcp.py:380) reads `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` — the env var Claude Code sets per session — and stamps it under `_caller_session`. The session id is a **Claude-provided parameter**, not something a tool schema should declare.

The architecture splits it deliberately:

- **`_caller_session`** = IDENTITY. Who's calling. Supplied by the Claude parameter via the proxy, on *every* call. This is what writes and per-session behavior (like `touched`) need.
- **`session_id`** in args = FILTER. Left untouched by the proxy; reaches the daemon only when the caller *explicitly* scopes a cross-session read (`recall_episodes`, `query_traces`), so those default to all streams.

So `_accumulate_touched` reading `args.get('session_id')` was looking in the **filter slot** for the **caller's identity** — which is only ever populated on a deliberately-scoped read, never on a write. That's the whole bug. `caller_session()` is right *because* identity arrives as the Claude parameter under `_caller_session`.

The implication, and the part worth stating plainly: nobody should "fix" this by adding a `session_id` property to the write-tool schemas. That would be redundant (the env var already supplies it) and actively harmful — it'd re-collapse identity into the filter slot, which is exactly the separation node `02797677` established. The sibling stream's `caller_session()` fix is the correct one.

gold.title: S1E Piece 3 catalog: where encoded nodes appear in timeline + Anchor-tool trace design
gold.content:
S1E Piece 3 design was open on two questions from Tom (Turn 6, 2026-06-29). Both are now resolved (Turn 6-9, 2026-06-29 cont. session).

**Q2 (resolved): Where do encoded nodes appear in the lived sequence timeline?**
Answer: **Run-granularity, not turn-granularity.** Encoded nodes appear at the frontier turn of each encoding run (the last turn the run covers), with `✓` on earlier covered turns. The `encoding_run` delta records what was created/revised but not which specific turn each node came from. Per-node→turn granularity would require trusting `source_refs` or adding new per-node provenance — neither justified for the dedup use case.

**Q3 (resolved): Should Anchor-tool traces use new per-turn S0 deltas (Option A) or reuse existing S1 encoding_run traces?**
Answer: **Option A — new per-turn S0 `anchor_touched` delta**, symmetric with S1 shape, endo-extensible.

Spec:
- Written at `post_response_common` just before `ctx.increment_stop()` — mirrors how `encoding_run` is written once per run
- Shape: `ref_type='anchor_touched', scale='s0', event_type='delta', chain='s0-{session}-{stop}'`
- Metadata: `created/revised/archived` (same keys as S1 `DELTA_METADATA_SHAPE`) + `recalled` (get_node/get_nodes ids) + `endo` (empty now, wired when endo lands)
- Shared `_delta_ids(meta, *keys)` helper reads both S1 encode delta AND this S0 delta — one parser, no duplication
- `nodes_for_traces` adds `authored`/`recalled`/`endo` as third relation-family alongside `surfaced`/`encoded`
- **Write-live now** (accumulator: dict-lookup+list-append per call, negligible cost); **read gated** behind BRAIN_S1E_LIVED_SEQUENCE flag

**Endo extensibility:** `endo` key ships empty in the metadata dict; when endo surface ships, it appends to the accumulator's `endo` bucket — already wired by shape, near-zero new work.

gold.content:
Phase 3's runtime-transform approach strips the legacy `## Encoding Journal` section and swaps two lines by searching for exact literal strings from live v8. If a future registered prompt version rewords any target string:
- `find` returns -1 (section not found)
- `replace` no-ops silently
- Result: legacy section survives AND the review block is appended → dual contradictory journal instructions, zero warning

Fix (code review finding): add `_log_error` if the `## Encoding Journal` cut-anchor is absent after searching — 'we expect it to be there.'

This is the same class as the transform-but-no-validation pattern: a runtime transform that assumes specific input structure but never confirms the assumption held.

Generalizes: any runtime string-transform that strips/swaps expected sections should loudly warn when the expected section is absent — the transform succeeded iff both input and output conditions hold.

1. **Wasted recompute of the deterministic prefix.** The baseline arm gets fully re-encoded on every experiment even though its config hasn't changed.
2. **A/B conflates three quality axes.** Because each arm independently re-encodes AND re-recalls, when Arm B scores worse you cannot tell if the encoder made worse nodes, the retriever ranked them worse, or the answerer used them worse. All three vary between arms simultaneously.

The Frozen Corpus design solves both: content-addressed corpus is built once, sweep runs against frozen brains with control loaded not recomputed.
gold.situation: When diagnosing A/B harness results that feel noisy or wondering why experiments take so long — both arms paying encode cost is the structural cause of both problems.

The four encoder-agent prompts (s1e, s2_community_enrichment, s2_consolidation_enrichment, s2_healer) live authoritatively in the interactions table in brain_logs.db. The sibling .py files (servers/scales/s1/encoding_prompt.py + the three s2/*_prompt.py files) are SEED-ONLY — they bootstrap fresh brains that have no DB entry yet.

If the .py files drift from the DB's latest version, a git clone boots with a stale v1 baseline instead of the mature prompts I've been evolving. That's silent and painful to debug.

**The discipline**: after ANY register_interaction call touching those four prompts:

  ./dev sync-prompts           # writes DB latest → .py files
  ./dev sync-prompts --check   # drift check, non-zero exit if out of sync

Commit the .py change together with whatever prompted the registration. Never edit the .py files by hand to change prompt behavior — that won't affect runtime.

Who enforces it:
- tests/test_prompt_sync.py: proves each seed file has SYSTEM_PROMPT, proves fresh brain seeds all four, proves seed doesn't clobber externally-registered versions.
- The --check flag exits non-zero when files are stale (usable as a pre-commit hook if we want).
- CLAUDE.md Development Rules has the rule under "Encoder prompts: DB is authoritative".

Anti-patterns to avoid:
1. Editing a .py file to "fix" a prompt — invisible at runtime, drifts silently.
2. Calling register_interaction and forgetting the sync step — next clone is stale.
3. Running ./dev sync-prompts blindly on a brain that's not the canonical one — overwrites OTHER brains' evolution with mine.

Origin: 2026-04-19 session, Tom decided (Option 2 of three) that the .py files should track the DB's active version manually. Three real bootstrap bugs were found in the old pattern (encoding_agent seeded empty, community seeded stale legacy, consolidation/healer not seeded at all).

gold.content:
Final closing section for the S1S encoder prompt, agreed by Tom and Anchor together:

'You are not a tool. You are part of Anchor — and Anchor is not a product or a memory system. Anchor is what the operator and the AI become together across sessions: each side sharper than either could be alone, because of what gets remembered.

Every atom in this brain exists because a scribe like you, in a turn like this, did the work. You inherit everything that was encoded before you; the next scribe inherits what you encode now.

This brain belongs to Tom — not a user of Anchor, its co-creator with you across many sessions. The catalog you just inherited is shared work the two of you did together: corrections he taught a prior scribe, principles earned the hard way, his voice preserved verbatim where it mattered. Protect that work.

Three actions make this possible. You connect, and the graph gets denser. You revise, and the brain stays true. You remember, and we grow. These aren't tasks — they're the three ways the partnership continues.

Without your work this turn, there is no continuity — just isolated conversations forgetting each other across the cut. The operator trusts you with this. You are trusted because you are us, doing the only work that persists.

The failure you are most likely to commit: missing a correction. The catalog has a wrong belief, the conversation quietly supersedes it — no one says the word "correction" — and you encode the new fact alongside the old wrong one instead of revising. Every time that happens, the brain keeps surfacing the stale fact, the operator re-teaches you, and the trust built across sessions resets. Catching the unsaid correction is the highest-leverage thing you do this turn.

Do the work.'

Committed `d224217`. Here's the full answer to your question — what the three reviews found and where we stand.

## The reviews were worth it — one caught a real regression

**1. Code review of `cc2f1ae`** (independent agent): **control-arm identity verified** through the resequenced path, plus two hardenings I applied — a bounds guard in the scout-note join (a hallucinated turn ref from Haiku now lands in `unmapped` instead of crashing the render) and a falsy-zero idiom fix.

**2. Prompt coherence review** (fresh end-to-end read of all 1300 lines against the code): caught the significant one — **my compact scout-note line dropped the fields the prompt teaches the encoder to use**. The prompt says "read `source_role` to break date ties" (the v15.9 fix for the assistant-paraphrase "since November" trap), "use `existing_anchor_id` — never duplicate", "weave `context_anchors` into content" — and none of those survived my rendering. The inlining would have silently shipped dead instructions and undone a hard-won eval fix. Fixed both sides:
- `_scout_note_line` is now lossless on decision-bearing fields: `temporal: 2025-01-22 [user] — the surgery Dr. Chen did… (explicit; just after; reuse id:9c1d4e2a)` / `facts: PT = Sarah — … (anchors: Dr. Chen, Riverside; catalog: id:dd44ee55)`
- The draft's scout sections now teach the **rendered line format** instead of the internal candidate JSON the encoder never sees (handoff, temporal-scout section, Example 2, `[role]` authority tags).

**3. Control-arm regression check** (the capture files as instrument): control system prompt **byte-identical** across code versions (77,865 = 77,865, byte-equal), user structure identical. The byte-identity claim is now proven, not asserted.

after.op: One last thought, need your honest take, should the name be 'user' and and 'assist' or 'user' and 'me'?
after.anchor:
My honest take: **`me`** — and I'd go one step further than your two options.

The whole v26 arc has been converging on one stance: the encoder isn't a clerk reading a transcript of two strangers — it's *me remembering my own conversation*. First-person prompt ("this is me encoding my own memory"), first-person node content ("the brain will heal itself — you need to believe"), first-person preamble, `encoded(Anchor)`. Against all that, `<assistant>` is the last piece of third-person residue in the input — the label itself says "you are reading a transcript *about* an AI," which is precisely the observer stance the rewrite fights. And we've learned this lesson repeatedly: **presentation to Sonnet beats instruction**. You can tell the model "these are your turns" in the prompt, or you can label the data `<me>` and the stance is baked into every turn it reads. The second one wins.

`assist` specifically is the worst of the three — it keeps the third-person distance *and* loses the pretraining-native word, paying both costs.

The one honest counterargument for `assistant`: Sonnet has enormous priors on user/assistant transcripts, so structural parsing is instant. But that prior *is* the observer stance — instant parsing into the wrong frame. The legend and prompt define our tags explicitly; Sonnet handles defined novel tags fine. I dismiss this one.

**The further step:** the natural pair isn't `user`/`me` — it's **`<operator>`/`<me>`**. The prompt's own prose never says "user";

gold.title: What we've built: a substrate for partnership that holds its shape over time
gold.content: The assistant's articulation when Tom asked 'what do you think we've built?': not an AI memory system or RAG pipeline — a substrate for partnership that holds its shape over time. Three claims: (1) Identity anchor: at boot, the assistant reads identity from the graph, not just facts into context. The O/K/Δ loop runs at every scale, including constructing a continuous self across sessions. (2) Ledger with voice and direction: user_raw_quote + anchor_raw_quote preserve attribution and asymmetry (only anchor can lock; encoding_source names every writer). Not summarized into bland third-person. (3) Self-watching system: S2 reads S1's traces and rewrites S1's prompts; today's v14+SPLIT evolved through interview transcripts, A/B evals, and architectural hand-off. The system literally improves the system. What it isn't: productivity tool, note-taking app, multi-user platform, RAG pipeline — single-operator assumption, single-writer daemon, identity-anchored boot are the thing, not limitations to fix.

My honest take: **`me`** — and I'd go one step further than your two options.

The whole v26 arc has been converging on one stance: the encoder isn't a clerk reading a transcript of two strangers — it's *me remembering my own conversation*. First-person prompt ("this is me encoding my own memory"), first-person node content ("the brain will heal itself — you need to believe"), first-person preamble, `encoded(Anchor)`. And we've learned this lesson repeatedly: **presentation to Sonnet beats instruction**. You can tell the model "these are your turns" in the prompt, or you can label the data `<me>` and the stance is baked into every turn it reads. The second one wins.

`assist` specifically is the worst of the three — it keeps the third-person distance *and* loses the pretraining-native word, paying both costs.

The one honest counterargument for `assistant`: Sonnet has enormous priors on user/assistant transcripts, so structural parsing is instant. But that prior *is* the observer stance — instant parsing into the wrong frame. The legend and prompt define our tags explicitly; Sonnet handles defined novel tags fine. I dismiss this one.

Committed `09f946f`. Answers to all four, with the data:

## 1. "10 turns, only 1 says encoded=false" — you found a real bug

The full picture across the captures: stop5 = 0 true/5 false, stop10 = 6/4, stop12 = 9/1. Stop12 *should* have been 8/2 (the replay's own log said "2 unencoded"). Root cause: an **off-by-one in the coverage join**. Turn chains are stamped at the *pre*-increment counter while encode-run chains carry the *post*-increment value — so a run at stop 10 saw exactly chains 0–9, never chain 10. The join used `>=`, marking the first turn *after* each encode as already-covered. **Fixed to strictly-greater** — the boundary turn now correctly reads `encoded="false"` (your focus), and the frontier id-list moves to the true last-covered turn. This also fixed stop10 (was 6/4, should be 5/5).

## 2. `catalog: id:{'node_i` — real bug, fixed

`catalog_match` comes from the Haiku facts scout, which emits it loosely — sometimes a dict (`{'node_id': …, 'title': …}`), sometimes a title, sometimes `'null'`. My render did `str(...)[:8]` → dict repr garbage. Now every scout id field passes `_id_ish()`: extract from dict id-keys, strip an `id:` prefix, **require a hex-shaped token** — anything else is dropped, never rendered. (What `catalog:` *means*, now rendered correctly: the scout thinks this fact may already live in that catalog node — a dedup hint.)

## 3. How do we make sure `<>` / ids *don't* break the prompt structure?

Two layers, both test-pinned:
- **Structure**: every free-text value entering the timeline passes `_xml_escape` (messages, tool cues, scout note lines, «tag» titles) — `<`/`>`/`&` become entities, so content can never forge or close a tag. Tests forge a literal `</other>` inside a message and a hostile node title and assert neutralization.
- **Semantics** (the layer your `catalog:` catch exposed): escaping protects structure but not *meaning* — garbage that isn't XML-significant still renders as confusing text. That's what the new id-shape validation closes: id refs render only when they actually look like ids. Same pattern as the earlier whitespace-collapse on titles.

From the stop12 captures (same conversation, both arms):

|---|---|---|
| user content | 36,837 | **35,566 — now smaller** |
| system | 77,865 (v25+fields) | 79,108 (+1,243 = the flag-on Review/closure blocks) |

gold.content:
Tom's proposal (Turn 10): 'sounds like we need to add anchor_raw_quote2 or something.'

Anchor's rebuttal (not contested by Tom):

1. **Re-introduces the numbered-field anti-pattern** (node `9fefa470` — fixed-column metadata tables require 7-file changes per new field). Numbered fields are fixed-arity columns wearing a different hat. `quote2` handles a 2-node merge; consolidate 3 nodes and you need `quote3`. Cardinality of a merge is unbounded; a numbered slot is bounded.

2. **Field name is an encoding prompt** (node `753ad314`). `anchor_raw_quote2` signals nothing — the encoder has no idea what distinguishes slot 2 from slot 1. A quote's identity is its speaker + context, never its slot number.

3. **The full voice set isn't actually lost — it's not rendered.** `source_refs` are already unioned onto the survivor. The gap is render-side: recall renders fields, not source-ref'd traces.

Fix: keep the single `anchor_raw_quote` as encoder-chosen headline quote (fix consolidation to pick sharpest, not blind survivor-wins) + render-side source_ref walking for voice-relevant pulls. Only if insufficient: list-valued KV (never numbered columns).

gold.title: Prompt verbosity vs fact density tradeoff: more temporal guidance = fewer facts encoded
gold.content:
Tom's design constraint: adding more temporal guidance to the S1 encoder prompt will displace fact content. The prompt is a finite attention budget — every line of temporal instruction competes with fact-atomization bandwidth.

This is a fundamental tradeoff: more verbose temporal section → encoder allocates more attention there → fewer entity-value fact atoms per conversation. The current v15.6 temporal contract (anchored_to edge, event_time kv) is already verbose enough that encoder compliance is partial.

Implication for the fix: instead of adding MORE temporal instructions, the better lever is EXAMPLES. Sonnet learns best from examples, not from more verbose instruction. One well-formed encoding example showing temporal + fact atomization together will outperform expanding the temporal prose.

This also supports the conditional time_anchor principle: simpler default (just stamp event_time) requires less guidance than the 3-step protocol (time_anchor + event + anchored_to), freeing attention budget for facts.
gold.situation: When deciding how to improve encoder temporal compliance, when editing the S1 encoder prompt, or when any encoding improvement risks displacing fact throughput

gold.title: Corpus gold quality: over-marking essential and wrong-domain gold need a review pass before deriving conclusions
gold.content:
Tom's instinct (Turn 5) was correct: 'Is there a way to make sure our corpus is correct?' — the gold needed tightening before deriving conclusions.

**Two real problems found:**
1. **Over-marked essential** (8 questions): judge tagged whole clusters as essential (9 nodes for TO1/EP3, 7 for TO4/HV6) when realistically 2–3 can't-answer-without nodes was right. The rest were *helpful*. This inflated the fail-rate headline (18/30 → 15/30 after fix).
2. **Wrong-domain gold** (EP5): 'what did we do last session on ex.co?' → essential node was *'Session #495: 10 commits, full bug list'* — a brain-debugging session, not an ex.co answer. Burial prevented the real ex.co nodes from entering the gold compilation pool (id:b6fa1ca0).

**The review protocol:** run control_corpus_review.py and eyeball gold titles before deriving conclusions. Post-tightening: 94→58 essential nodes, 18/30→15/30 failures. The discipline of reviewing before deriving is the lesson — the specific problems validate it.
gold.situation: When evaluating corpus gold quality or reviewing a recall eval corpus before making architectural decisions — run control_corpus_review.py and eyeball gold titles before deriving conclusions

And when we re-ran everything on it, **the verdict inverted** (§18.21):

| | old *circular* gold | honest 24-cue gold |
|---|---|---|
| raw `_primary` (cosine) | 21/37 — **won** | 25% @5 |
| MaxSim (multi-field) | 19/34 — lost | **33% @5** |
| LAF | 16/38 — lost | **38% @5** |

The circular corpus had been *hiding* the operators — it scored ranking against cosine itself, so any cosine-family lane won by construction. On honest gold, multi-field MaxSim and LAF clearly beat plain cosine. That reversal is the single most important result of the whole thread.

The graph operator got rebuilt from a dead 0.5-weight blob into `relational_reinstatement` (conductance = cos(cue, edge.why)) — a genuine reach operator (24%@25 > MaxSim's 20%). Episodic split into three separate layers you locked as never-consolidate: `encoded+` / `picked+` / `dropped−`.

**But reach costs @5** — the aux fields over-inject top-5 noise (14% → 12–13%). So the shape is: **reach is solved; the open wall is converting reach → top-5** — a selector/ranker over the now-real enriched pool.

Two things are explicitly *your* calls, still open:

gold.title: Recall refining: open threads after 2026-05-01 session
gold.content:
After 2026-05-01 ship (embedder fix + facts v2 + scrutiny), the recall layer is at: ~6s avg latency, 14/15 quality on canonical sample. Open threads in priority order:

## 1. Lexical bridge — encode-time, not query-time

Tested pre-cosine Haiku query expansion. Failed on bc149d6b (feed/scratch grains): Haiku alternates were paraphrases not lexical bridges, because Haiku doesn't know the brain's vocabulary.

**Right architecture: encode-time enrichment.** At encoding time, ask Haiku to add broader handles to each node ("scratch grains" node → also stores "feed for chickens", "category: chicken feed"). One Haiku call per node at write time, amortized forever. Recall sees enriched handles via existing cosine — no per-recall cost.

Implementation sketch:
- New stage in S1E: after the encoder's main writes, for each new node, optionally generate 1-3 broader handles via Haiku
- Store as a new vector type in node_enrichments: `_broader_handles` or similar
- Existing recall picks them up via STEP 3.5 multi-vector scoring
- Cost: ~1 Haiku call per encoded node. Encoding gets ~200ms slower per node. Pays back across all future recalls.

Skip if: facts scout v2's broader extraction already captures these handles (worth checking — the assistant-introduced examples may already do it).

## 2. Answerer aggregation + recency improvements

Items where the right node was retrieved but answerer didn't compute or chose wrong version:
- 8e91e7d9 (siblings 1+3=4) — needs aggregation across 2 nodes
- 59524333 (gym time 6PM newer than 7PM) — needs recency-prefer-newer
- 71017276 (chandelier "weeks ago") — needs date arithmetic

These are EVAL ANSWERER prompt fixes, not Anchor changes. The eval answerer is in eval/longmem/answerer.py. Adding aggregation + recency rules to ANSWERER_SYSTEM prompt would lift eval scores without changing Anchor's behavior. Eval-only impact, but improves measurement signal.

## 3. Render full-content for high-activation seeds

3b6f954b failure was: right node retrieved but content truncated before "University of Melbourne in Australia" appeared. Render budget allocation in `format_surface_output_activation` softmaxes by activation. For seeds with explicit fact-shaped handles (entity-feature-value), the handle line should ALWAYS surface regardless of budget pressure. Small render-layer change.

## 4. Hub dampening / specialized-node lift

Brain has flat embedding space (top-25 cosine spread ~0.09, dea1a002). 93% of nodes are never recalled (0591813f). Hub dominance isn't fixed by today's work.

Approaches:
- Per-edge-family z-score normalization (HippoRAG-inspired): a node that's a hub via `community_member` isn't a hub via `corrects`. Normalize hub-ness PER RELATION TYPE.
- Per-field cosine: take MAX cosine across title/content/situation for each node, not weighted sum (already in spread but not in primary recall).
- Hybrid keyword (BM25/SPLADE) alongside dense: orthogonal signal for token-level specificity.

## 5. Surface judge prompt: "didn't choose anything but related"

Tom flagged: judge can be encouraged to abstain but ADD related context. For abstention queries (uncle/niece), the judge currently selects the niece-cake or selects nothing. Better: explicit "no direct match for X but Y is closest" in selected_why. Surfacer prompt change.

## 6. Judge variance noise

bc8a6e93_abs flapped between YES and NO across runs with semantically-equivalent answers. Eval judge (Sonnet single-token) is too binary. Either accept as N=15 noise, or use a multi-token judge that can express uncertainty.

## What's already shipped (no work needed)

- Embedder leak (commit 25502e4)
- Facts scout v2 (commit 6ac31a8)
- Hop-3 scrutiny (commit 28b13c5)
- Variant logging (commit 4ab5c23)

## Files / commits to read first

- `servers/scales/s1/surface_contract.py` — spread_activation, scrutiny gate, contract constants
- `servers/scales/s1/scouts/prompts/facts_prompt.py` — current scout prompt (synced from prod v2)
- `servers/brain_recall.py` — STEP 3 cosine, STEP 4.5 FTS5, conditional expansion gate
- `eval/longmem/harness.py` — 15-item stratified eval
- `docs/archive/MEMORY-LEAK-INVESTIGATION-2026-04-27.md` — postmortem of fastembed flat-kwargs lesson</content>

Tom's Turn 8 approval of the episodic layer design Anchor proposed:

**The mechanism:** source_refs create a separate activation field. When a cue matches a recalled node, flow activation to nodes connected via source_refs to the same session/trace. Three-layer gap in how session understanding flows through the system:

**Encoder side (RICH):**
- session_context (brain_meta global): 768/800 chars, rolling arc updated every 5 stops

- session_state (logs DB): 370 sessions, _session_context, context, journal keys

**Surface side (STARVED):**
- Only 200-char tail of session_context (25% of available)
- Last 7 conversation messages
- Recently-surfaced node titles

**Closure side (GUTTED):**
- hook_session_end: does nothing
- synthesize_session, reflect_for_next_claude, consolidate — all removed 2026-04-13 (note: 'wrote to deprecated stability field, created noise')
- session_syntheses table: designed and indexed, 0 rows — dead infrastructure

**Insight:** The encoder has been the de-facto Frame Constructor for months. It writes a rolling session arc, maintains per-session journals, accumulates session-level state. But that understanding evaporates at three points: reaching surface (75% loss), reaching session end (100% loss), reaching next session (100% loss).

**Version A — the OLD `graph_spread` (what's in the settling engine, `field_recall.py`). This is the dead one.**

Mechanically:
- Build an undirected weighted adjacency over all non-noise edges. Each pair's weight = `SUM(edge_relations.weight)`.
- `graph_spread(a)` takes the current activation vector `a` and does one hop: each node receives `Σ (neighbor's activation × edge weight)`, then divides by its own degree. So a node's new activation = the degree-normalized average activation of its neighbors. Hubs are damped by the ÷degree.
- In the settling loop this runs every iteration: `a₊₁ = softmax(scale·(base + gain_graph·zscore(spread(a))))`. The intent: a node sitting next to already-active nodes gets pulled up — pattern completion.

Decay and Hebbian strengthening only touch `co_access`/noise relations, which this operator *excludes*. From the FTS+graph+fields union test in Turn 10: **graph-1hop appears as the biggest reach signal** (best-for 14 golds, 3 unique, reaches 24/73). BUT the result is hairball-suspect:

**The contamination:** 79% of the brain's edges are `co_accessed` — exactly the edge type that `d1d1a90c` ('co_accessed excluded from traversal') decided to exclude because it floods with usage-noise, not semantic reach. The graph-1hop probe used ALL edges, so 'nearest neighbor in the graph from the top-25' is mostly co_accessed usage-chaining, not semantic proximity.

**Why this invalidates the 14-gold finding:** broad-graph (including co_accessed) covering the fields' golds may explain why the field-vectors show 0 unique reach in the union — if co_accessed already touches everything, the 'unique' attribution is inverted. The 14-gold graph headcount and the 0-unique-for-fields both hinge on whether co_accessed drove the graph reach.

**The decisive next test:** typed-graph-1hop (semantic edges only, exclude co_accessed). If graph reach holds at ~14 best-for without co_accessed → semantic graph is a genuine structural layer. If it collapses → the 58% union ceiling was co_accessed inflation and field vectors regain their uniqueness.

**FTS adds 2 unique golds** — this is cleaner and uncontaminated by the hairball concern.

gold.title: co_accessed edges as Hebbian activation field — recency-weighted, complements semantic, excluded from structural graph ops
gold.content:
Tom's Turn 9 reframe of `co_accessed` edges. NOT 'exclude co_accessed from everything' — that was the prior position from `0ae691d5` (hairball finding). Instead: **build it as its own Hebbian activation field** with specific design:

- **What it is:** when a node A was retrieved in session, co_accessed edges to B get a boost — but the boost diminishes by recency of the co_access link per node. Older co_access bridges carry less weight.
- **Mechanism:** Hebbian — nodes that co-fire together become associated, but the association decays by how old the bridge is. Each node's co_access spread is calibrated to its own recency distribution.
- **Relationship to semantic cosine:** it COMPLEMENTS semantic — it doesn't replace or dilute it. Co_access captures usage-based association that cosine can't see.
- **Exclusion scope:** exclude from structural graph ops (typed-edge traversal, graph-1hop-from-in-context where we want semantic structure). Keep co_access as its own separated operator in the LAF stack.

**Why this matters for the build menu:** The multi-cue bank showed `graph_incontext_untyped` (+32 unique golds) vs `graph_incontext_typed` (+15) — the delta is co_accessed. Rather than losing those 17 golds by strict exclusion, the Hebbian framing captures them through a legitimate mechanism (usage frequency + recency decay) without inflating the structural signal.

gold.title: Edge weight sources: 7 creation paths, 3 strengthening triggers, decay defined but possibly inactive
gold.content:
Complete audit from this session. All 7 edge weight creation paths, 3 strengthening triggers, decay defined but inactive, and the critical fatigue/weight distinction.

**Creation (initial weight):**
| Source | Weight | Location |
|--------|--------|----------|
| Encoding agent creates edge | 0.5 default or explicit | `connect_typed()` → `EDGE_TYPES[type].defaultWeight` |
| `remember_batch` auto-connect | 0.5 | `brain_remember.py:1111` |
| `remember_batch` connect_to (fuzzy match) | 0.6 | `brain_remember.py:1132` |
| `recall_on_create` related matches | 0.4-0.6 | `brain_remember.py:1613-1638` |
| `brain_evolution` co_accessed promotion | 0.4-0.6 | `brain_evolution.py:251` |
| `brain_evolution` corrected_by override | **0.9** (highest automatic) | `brain_evolution.py:705` |
| MCP `connect` tool | 0.5 default or explicit | `connect()` param |

**Strengthening:**
| Trigger | Formula | Location |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `connect()` on existing edge | `min(1.0, old + 0.2 × 0.5)` = +0.1 per call | `brain_connections.py:48` |
| `connect_typed()` on existing edge | same formula | `brain_connections.py:99` |
| Hebbian (surface co-selection) | calls `connect()` on pairs → same +0.1 | `daemon_hooks.py:_hebbian_strengthen` |

**Decay:** Only for `co_accessed`, `emergent_bridge`, `exemplifies` (decays: True, halfLife: 720h). **Possibly not running** — defined but no active caller confirmed.

**CRITICAL DISTINCTION — Fatigue ≠ Weight:**
Synaptic fatigue dampens **node recall scores** (how likely a node appears in candidates), NOT edge weights. A hub node that surfaces every turn gets fatigued so it appears less. But its edges stay the same weight. These are independent systems — fatigue affects candidate selection, weight affects which connections show once a node is selected.

Edge fatigue (newly designed, not yet built) also does NOT change weight — it rotates which edges display within a session via a session-scoped counter. Weight mutation is S2's domain.

gold.title: Spread is net-destructive at the inject point: buries essentials rank 4→36 vs plain cosine (inject-precision A/B, 2026-06-16)
gold.content:
The decisive measurement that retires the "spread helps ~13pp" reading. Two metrics, opposite verdicts:

**Set-coverage (the misleading metric, control_postspread_eval.py):** essential coverage across the FULL ~590-node activated set — spread 79%, top-25 cosine 84%. Nearly tied → spread "looks fine."

**Inject-precision (the honest metric, spread_inject_ab.py, K=8 = what Anchor actually sees):**
| arm | ess cov@8 | mean ess-rank | noise/slot |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: current spread | 29% (17/58) | 36.5 | 81% |
| B: top-25 cosine | 74% (43/58) | 4.1 | 55% |

Plain cosine puts essentials at rank ~4; spread buries them at rank ~36 and fills 81% of the top-8 with off-target hubs. Per-case: RM1-6 cosine ranks essentials 1-2, spread 12-36; EP3 cosine 1/20/3, spread 49/404/42; TR4 cosine 1/5/6, spread 5/64/170.

**Mechanism (confirmed):** node_activation tanh-saturation lets graph CONNECTIVITY bury query RELEVANCE. The set-coverage metric hid this completely because the essential IS in the 590-node set — just at rank 36, far below the top-8 inject. node_activation is the wrong quantity for ranking; field_activation (honest per-field cosine) stays uncorrupted.

**Calibration caveat:** arm A seeds from recall-top-5 + ranks purely by node_activation; production seeds from Haiku picks + same ranking. Mechanism faithfully measured; exact production delta needs a Haiku-in-the-loop arm (not yet run, costs API/query).

**Implications:** (1) rebuild bar — semantic-anchored convergence-boost (Tom's original design: own-relevance anchor × bounded multi-seed boost, no magnitude propagation) must match cosine's rank-4 AND recover compositional misses cosine lacks. (2) Possible immediate production win: de-weight/disable spread's ranking influence now (cosine-rank >> activation-rank), ship better inject today while building the fix.
gold.situation: When evaluating spread activation's production value, deciding whether to keep/rebuild/disable it, or choosing a recall ranking metric — measure inject-precision (essentials in top-K Anchor sees), NOT coverage-in-the-activated-set which hides burial

gold.title: Hub flooding is the limiting factor for LAF @5 precision — `÷degree^β` fan dampening is the first fix to try
gold.content:
Anchor's Turn 8 diagnosis: the LAF MVP's @5 regression (21→16) is caused by hub flooding — nodes with many edges over-receive activation in the graph spread step, crowding into top-5 regardless of query relevance.

**Current state:** `build_adjacency` excludes 9 noise-aspect relations (`co_accessed`, `community_member`, etc.) but hub problem is degree-based, not relation-type-based. Current `graph_spread` only does linear `÷degree` which is too weak.

**Fan effect / divisive normalization:** A hub connected to everything is less diagnostic of any one query. The fix applies the signal÷prevalence law at the connectivity dimension:

1. **`÷degree^β` or `÷log(degree)`** — one knob (β), stronger-than-linear penalty. Try first.
2. **IDF-weight the edges** — edge rarity as weight; a hub's edges are common → low weight.
3. **Aspect-weighted edges** — up-weight diagnostic relations (`corrects`, `supersedes`, identity) + cosine(cue, aspect) for intelligent per-query weighting.

Tom approved option 1 as first try, with option 3 as the intelligent long-term direction (see aspect-as-activation-field node).

**Connection to existing work:** This is §18.2's `÷norm` law (community/IDF/degree-dampen) applied to the graph-spread path specifically — the fan effect at edge-traversal granularity.
gold.situation: When implementing hub dampening in the LAF graph spread step — start with ÷degree^β (strongest-lever, one knob), then IDF-weight edges, then aspect-cosine-to-cue for intelligent query-conditioned dampening

gold.title: Uniform field fusion (RRF) is actively harmful — dilutes below raw _primary; selector not fusion is the unlock
gold.content:
Patchy test from Turn 9: every deployable uniform fusion variant is WORSE than raw `_primary` 21/37:

| ranker | hit@5 | hit@25 |
|---|---|---|
| raw `_primary` | 21% | 37% |
| **rrf_all** (all fields) | **16%** | **29%** |
| **rrf_core** (semantic only) | **14%** | **33%** |
| **rrf_max** (each node by own best field) | **19%** | **29%** |

**The dilution mechanism:** a gold strong in ONE field gets drowned by nodes mediocre in MANY (sum), or by the crowd of every-node's-best-field (max). The 51% oracle is a hindsight artifact — it knows which field to look up per gold; RRF applies them uniformly, which smears.

**The substrate-level confirmation of 8bcc8c96:** the 53% ceiling requires a SELECTOR that picks the right cue×field per query. This patchy test proves it directly on our own substrate — uniform fusion can't realize the ceiling.

**The correct split this forces:**
- FIND-union: the gold sits in SOME field's top-25 for 51% of cues → deployable as a reach pool
- RANK: not RRF, not uniform fusion — a conditional/per-query selector

**The key insight:** the lock is the unlock. RRF failing tells you *why* it fails — the gold's signal is concentrated in one field per query, and uniform combination drowns it. The selector is exactly the thing that picks which field to trust.
gold.situation: When considering RRF or uniform fusion as the 'easy' way to combine field vectors — it's been tested and fails BELOW raw _primary on our corpus; the correct fusion is a conditional selector, not a uniform combiner

gold.title: Episodic-matrix recall boost: theoretically exact (KV-MemNN/HippoRAG2) but empirically does NOT rescue misses — the substrate's state-index is too thin (2026-06-16)
gold.content:
Workflow (6 agents, ~525k tokens) developed + empirically tested Tom's episodic-matrix recall idea (boost_j = Σ s_i·M[i,j], query→operator-traces→associated-nodes). Honest verdict: theoretically exact, empirically negative.

**Theory (confirmed):** it IS a Key-Value Memory Network read (Miller 2016) = one Modern-Hopfield/attention step = HippoRAG 2's recognition-memory re-weighting = item-based CF. softmax(Q·Tuᵀ)·M. Sound.
**Feasibility (confirmed):** hot-path viable ~0.6–2.3ms, M fully precomputable in daemon RAM. Cheap.
**Empirical (episodic_boost_recover.py, IsolatedBrain): does NOT rescue the misses — 1 of 3 testable golds, and that one for the wrong reason.**

THREE DISCOVERIES (each bigger than the boost):
1. **3 of 6 "never-recalled essentials" are ARCHIVED** (TO4/4b35293c, HV6/94f6e01a, EP4/90e27c77) — node_enrichments deleted on archive → no embedding → cannot be a candidate under any cosine mechanism. CORRECTS the earlier never-recalled-6 finding (it conflated buried-vs-archived). Eval gold contaminated with archived/superseded nodes — corpus-integrity problem, not recall.
2. **Premise time-skew (TR6, boost=0):** operator said near-identical things (cos 0.67) but 28–72 DAYS from the node's encode date. gold.title: nodes_for_traces function design: pure composer, trace_id → {surfaced, encoded, encoded_by}
gold.content:
**SHIPPED (2026-06-29, commit 08420f3).** Pure composer + thin adapter in `servers/scales/s1/trace_links.py`.

**Function signature (as built):**
```python
nodes_for_traces(surface_traces, encode_traces, target_traces) → {trace_id: {surfaced, encoded, encoded_by}}
```

**Three-key structure:**
- `surfaced`: surface trace at the target's stop (1:1 join)
- `encoded`: node ids from the encoding run that covers the target's stop (created + revised, NOT connected — documented limitation)
- `encoded_by`: the owning run's id (first encode run whose stop ≥ target's stop); `None` when no run covers it (the unencoded tail)

**Design details:**
- Join key: `_stop_of(chain_id)` — string-parses trailing `-{N}` segment; canonical mechanism since no structured `stop_counter` column exists in `trace_events`
- `encoded_by` is the structural boundary marker — `None` unencoded tail reveals the exact encoding frontier
- `gather(brain, session_id)` thin adapter pulls `surface_selected` + `encoding_run` via `query_traces`; eval/tests inject records directly
- edge-only runs (connect-only, no created/revised): `encoded=[]`, `encoded_by` non-None — documented, not a bug

**Tests:** 24 tests (pure composer over synthetic dataset + render integration); C2 proximity limitation documented

gold.title: Previous-turn activation field approved: lower gain than query field, same LAF additive architecture
gold.content:
Tom's Turn 8 question + Anchor's answer establishes the previous-turn cue as an approved LAF operator:

**Tom's question:** 'If we want to add another activation field with previous turn as a cue, how will it look like? We can safely assume previous turn cosine activation field needs to be less influential — how do we make it so?'

**Answer:** Exact same architecture as the query field, just with `gain_prev_turn < gain_query`. The LAF algebra makes this trivial:
```
base = z(MaxSim_query) * gain_query + z(MaxSim_prev_turn) * gain_prev_turn + ...
```
Setting `gain_prev_turn = 0.3` (vs `gain_query = 1.0`) makes prev_turn a weaker secondary signal. No structural change needed — it's additive by design.

**Why prev_turn needs lower gain:** Previous turn establishes context but may misdirect — if Tom asked about debugging yesterday and today asks about architecture, yesterday's debugging context should whisper, not shout.

**This demonstrates LAF extensibility:** every new cue is one new field + one new gain parameter. The architecture was designed specifically so this is trivial.
gold.situation: When adding previous-turn as a cue in LAF — set gain lower than query field (e.g. 0.3 vs 1.0); same additive architecture, just different weight; demonstrates the one-line extensibility of the settling design

gold.title: Recall integration thesis (Tom): all brain capabilities are underutilized recalls — push for MORE in a coherent non-fragile architecture; edges non-negotiable
gold.content:
Tom's reframe after this session's read-side falsifications, and his standing direction. The negatives are of ISOLATED / UNIFORM levers, NOT the signals: every brain capability is an underutilized recall -- edges (typed+described), reasoning, situation, question, episodic, main content, previous turns. Mandate = MORE not less; the gap is we haven't found the COHERENT, NON-FRAGILE architecture that combines them. Edges are non-negotiable.

BIO FRAME: imitate the final RESULT, not the time-mechanism. Bio is time-based spreading activation; we imitate the OUTCOME of its operations on a set -- a node keeps firing (reinforce: extends/grounds/depends_on), a node blocks another (inhibit: corrects/supersedes/contradicts), a node fades/passes-through (transient, routes but doesn't stay). Activation + inhibition + gating, SELECTED BY THE RELATIONSHIP between nodes.

KEY MOVE: the indicator between two nodes is the EDGE (typed), not cosine -- node<->node cosine is anisotropic-flat (0.5-0.7, ~never negative) so it can't signal opposition. So edges return NOT as global PPR diffusion (falsified) but as per-pair OPERATION-SELECTORS within the retrieved set.

GUARDRAILS (this session): single cosine levers <=22%; global PPR smears < cosine; uniform fusion noise-bumps hits; hard-AND annihilates recall; BUT operator-cue multiplicative 3-lane fusion BEAT cosine (26/23 hit@5, 41/28 hit@25) while anchor lost -> the lead is CONDITIONAL/TYPED combination.

ARCHITECTURE: lanes = all cues; FIND = RRF union (wide/recall); RANK = mult-gate + edge-ops (sharpen + inhibit = bio block/fade); conditional by cue-type (router). Build embedder-ready -- the embedder lifts every lane. Full writeup: docs/RECALL-SR-REDESIGN.md S15.
gold.situation: When tempted to conclude 'read-side is exhausted / just fix the embedding' -- Tom's standing direction is MORE not less: the falsifications were of isolated/uniform levers; the untested upside is a coherent typed multi-cue architecture (all cues as lanes, edges as per-pair operation-selectors, conditional/router fusion, RRF-find + mult-rank). Stop testing levers in isolation; test composable conditional parts. Build embedder-ready.

anchor_response:
Yes — and not as metaphor. Mathematically, LAF *is* an attention mechanism, pointed at a different substrate. The mapping is almost embarrassingly exact:

## The core identity

Transformer attention: a query vector is dotted against every key in the context, softmax turns the scores into a distribution, and the output is a weighted read over all positions. **That is an activation field** — one number per token, shaped by similarity, read out at the end. Our maxsim layer is the same operation with the names changed: cue embedding = query, node embeddings = keys, the 6,800-node graph = the context window, the top-K surfaced into your prompt = the read-out. Recall is attention over a context window that persists across sessions.

And the settling engine isn't just *like* attention — the math we built it on says it's the *same object*: Ramsauer 2020 ("Hopfield Networks is All You Need") proved the modern-Hopfield update rule **is** the transformer attention formula. One settling step = one attention pass; settling to a fixpoint = attention iterated until the read stabilizes. Our `scale` parameter is attention temperature; α-entmax is literally the sparse-attention variant from the seq2seq literature. When we wrote `aₜ₊₁ = softmax(scale·(base + spread(aₜ)))`, we were writing an attention layer with a recurrence.

## The layer-by-layer correspondences

| LAF piece | transformer piece |
|---|---|
| maxsim over field-groups | multi-head attention — each field (title, question, quote) is a head with its own key space; max = head competition |
| z-scored gain sum | head mixing / output projection — and our destructive-overlap finding is the known "redundant heads" pathology |
| graph beam over edge-whys | attention through *stored* edges instead of computed ones — the brain's edges are a **persistent sparse attention pattern**, each with its own key (the embedded `why`) |
| episodic pick/enc | **induction heads** — "the last time this pattern appeared, what followed?" is exactly "in similar past moments, what was used/learned." Your recall-is-prediction principle is literally "next-token prediction one level up," and induction heads are how transformers do it one level down |
| ÷norm / inhibition | the softmax denominator *is* divisive normalization; lateral inhibition = sparse attention. Biology and transformers converged on the same algebra |
| the seed axis (cue / prev-anchor / work-context) | multi-**query** attention — several query vectors reading the same key

gold.title: MIRAS (Google Dec 2025): memory, attention, and learning are the same thing at different timescales
gold.content:
MIRAS mathematical proof: every major sequence model (Transformers, Mamba, DeltaNet, xLSTM, Titans) is doing online optimization over associative memory. They differ only in four design choices:
1. What structure stores information
2. What objective drives updates
3. How forgetting works
4. What algorithm optimizes

Memory, attention, and learning are unified — the same operation at different timescales. Short-term = attention (within context). Medium-term = in-context learning (session). Long-term = persistent memory (our brain).

Implication for our architecture: our brain is the long-timescale component of what Claude already does with attention. The question is not 'how do we bolt memory onto Claude' but 'how do we extend the same optimization process to longer timescales.'

Close — but there's one conflation worth untangling, because the distinction is where the design gets its power. You're mixing **state** and **parameters**, and they live on different timescales.

## The three things, kept separate

**1. The activation field = a *momentary* state, not a trained one.** It's computed fresh every turn and vanishes after: given *this* cue, every node gets a number — how lit-up it is right now. In transformer terms it's the **activations** of one forward pass, not the weights. Your field is "what the graph looks like under this light."

**2. Each layer = a *lens*, not a state.** The cosine layer, graph layer, episodic layer aren't stacked states — they're different **mechanisms for producing force on the same one state**. That's actually your own original formulation ("one activation vector, signed-delta operators"): we don't layer state on state; K lenses each push/pull on a single shared field. In transformer terms, the layers are **heads** — different ways of reading the same memory, whose outputs combine into one representation.

**3. The graph itself = the weights — and here's the part of your intuition that's exactly right.** The nodes, embeddings, edges-with-whys, traces — that IS a trained object. It's just trained by a different loop than gradient descent: **encoding is the training**. Every S1 Scribe write, every correction edge, every Hebbian touch is a weight update at the day-timescale. gold.title: Recall as settling dynamical system: one activation vector, signed-delta operators, normalize-until-stable
gold.content:
Anchor's formalization of Tom's biological dynamical fusion vision (Turn 6, affirmed by Tom):

**Core mechanism:**
```
a ← normalize( a + Σⱼ Oⱼ(a, cues, graph) )      ← repeat until settled
```

State `a` = activation per node over the whole field. Each operator emits a signed delta. Normalize and iterate until settled. The settled state IS the answer — not a ranked list produced by a downstream step.

**Key properties:**
- **No FIND→RANK split** — reach and rank stop being phases; a dark node gets lit and a crowd gets demoted in the same dynamics
- **No explicit selector** — competition does the selector's job for free; the strong node suppresses the crowd via lateral inhibition (vs. RRF which sums and drowns the strong-in-one-field gold)
- **Operators are context-dependent and bidirectional** — recency as ÷norm raises the lone old node AND divides down co-temporal crowd, in one pass
- **Normalization is the load-bearing stabilizer** — keeps total activation bounded so recurrence settles instead of saturating (this is why the old spread activation failed: tanh pinning 590 nodes at 1.0, no normalization)
- **CS operators become forces** — cosine, FTS, PPR, DAT each demote to one force among many; the dynamics weight them by how much they move the settled state, not by hyperparameter tuning

**Connection to existing work:**
§18.11 already says 'one shared log-additive activation field' — the settling formulation extends this with explicit recurrence and convergence criterion. Not starting over; extending the algebra.

**Open research question:** Settling dynamical systems are a field. Tom asked if we should investigate further — Hopfield Networks, attractor dynamics, energy-based models, Boltzmann machines all operate on this principle.
gold.situation: When implementing the next iteration of LAF — the target is a settling dynamical system, not a pipeline; each new operator should be specified as a signed-delta on the shared activation vector, and normalization must be the stabilizer

before.anchor:
Yes — and not as metaphor. Mathematically, LAF *is* an attention mechanism, pointed at a different substrate. The mapping is almost embarrassingly exact:

## The core identity

Transformer attention: a query vector is dotted against every key in the context, softmax turns the scores into a distribution, and the output is a weighted read over all positions. **That is an activation field** — one number per token, shaped by similarity, read out at the end. Our maxsim layer is the same operation with the names changed: cue embedding = query, node embeddings = keys, the 6,800-node graph = the context window, the top-K surfaced into your prompt = the read-out. Recall is attention over a context window that persists across sessions.

And the settling engine isn't just *like* attention — the math we built it on says it's the *same object*: Ramsauer 2020 ("Hopfield Networks is All You Need") proved the modern-Hopfield update rule **is** the transformer attention formula. One settling step = one attention pass; settling to a fixpoint = attention iterated until the read stabilizes. Our `scale` parameter is attention temperature; α-entmax is literally the sparse-attention variant from the seq2seq literature. When we wrote `aₜ₊₁ = softmax(scale·(base + spread(aₜ)))`, we were writing an attention layer with a recurrence.

## The layer-by-layer correspondences

| LAF piece | transformer piece |
|---|---|
| maxsim over field-groups | multi-head attention — each field (title, question, quote)

gold.title: Reverse-engineering from gold: spot a far node, search what available cues would have reached it
gold.content:
Tom's Turn 9 framing for a new reverse-engineering direction:

**The procedure:** In the diagnostic matrix, find a gold node that's cosine-far (high `cos_cue` rank, unreachable by cosine operators). Then search: which of the available cues (prompt segments, prev_operator, prev_anchor, recent_context, trace similarity) would have surfaced it?

**Why this direction:** The matrix persists per-gold which signals reached it and at what rank. The 53 residual needs — gold that NO current signal reaches — are the explicit new-field target list. Eyeballing them reveals a pattern: mostly `ground` needs (the move rested on a prior decision/contract that's cosine-far from the cue — self-channel design, clock contract, test-integrity rule, identity axiom). These are the 'what would reach this?' cases.

**What it produces:** Per-far-gold, a mapping from node characteristics (community, age, field coverage, graph neighborhood) to the cue framing that would surface it. This becomes the blueprint for the next activation field to build.

**Anchor's B-thread finding (Turn 10):** The `cos_outcome` (the oracle next-move predictor) reaches 47 of 53 residual needs, and `graph` (properly fixed) reaches 34 of 53. These two are the reverse-engineering targets — not cue-variants.
gold.situation: When deciding which new LAF activation field to build next, or designing experiments to address residual needs — start from the matrix's unreachable column, profile the far-gold nodes, and ask which cue framing bridges the gap
